short: Shoot-quality ads without the shoot. Made with AI, directed by you.
title: AI & ADVERTISING

doc.p:
Use
Student Kit: START-HERE

Do this now
Write down your brand and the one product you'll use for the whole course.

items.desc: An ad goes through 6 steps: Brief → Concept → Visuals → Motion → Edit → Launch. AI makes visuals, motion and edits fast. You bring the idea and the direction.
items.title: Where AI fits in every type of ad

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Student Kit: START-HERE
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Student Kit: START-HERE (Main tools)

Do this now
List the tool you'll use for each step, and which ones you already have.

items.desc: The stack: Flow for video and images, ChatGPT for images, Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini for thinking, ElevenLabs for voice, Suno for music, Claude for editing, Meta Ads Manager to launch.
items.title: Your AI ad stack and what it costs

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Student Kit: START-HERE (Main tools)
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Student Kit: START-HERE (How to attach a skill)

Do this now
Sign in to Google Flow and ChatGPT, make your project folder, and take your 5 product photos.

items.desc: Start on free plans and pay only when you hit a limit. Set up one project folder and use the file naming from day 1.
items.title: Setting up your tools the cheap way

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Student Kit: START-HERE (How to attach a skill)
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Strategist skill (policy check)

Do this now
Run the policy check in the Ad Strategist skill and write down one claim you must never make for your product.

items.desc: The rules: use AI tools on a plan that allows commercial use. No celebrity faces, no competitor logos, no fake results. Check Meta's AI labels and the ASCI guidelines on launch day.
items.title: Rules, rights and AI disclosure on Meta

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Strategist skill (policy check)
resources.title: Course Resources

modules.title: AI in advertising: the new playbook
modules.banner: Start here: open Course Resources and download the Student Kit. Every lesson tells you which skill and workflow to use.
modules.description: AI doesn't replace taste. It replaces the shoot.

doc.p:
Use
Ad Strategist (brief) · Workflow 01, steps 1–2

Do this now
Turn your brand's goal into a one-page creative brief.

items.desc: A brief has 5 things: goal, audience, one message, must-haves, how we measure. Turn a messy WhatsApp message into a one-page brief.
items.title: Reading a brief like an agency

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Strategist (brief) · Workflow 01, steps 1–2
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Strategist (big idea) · Workflow 01, step 3

Do this now
Get 3 big ideas for your product and pick one.

items.desc: Let AI read customer reviews and competitor ads (Meta Ad Library). Pick one angle: pain, desire, proof or festive.
items.title: Audience, angle and positioning with AI

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Strategist (big idea) · Workflow 01, step 3
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Strategist (hooks) · Workflow 01, step 4

Do this now
Write 30 hooks and keep your best 5.

items.desc: The hook is the first 2 seconds. Types: visual shock, question, bold claim, pattern break, offer. Write 30 and keep 5.
items.title: Hooks that stop the scroll

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Strategist (hooks) · Workflow 01, step 4
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Strategist (script & storyboard) · Workflow 01, steps 4–6

Do this now
Write a 15s script and a 6-frame storyboard, then build your Brand Bible.

items.desc: A 15s script goes hook → problem → product → proof → CTA. The storyboard has 6 frames, and each frame becomes an image prompt.
items.title: Writing scripts and storyboards

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Strategist (script & storyboard) · Workflow 01, steps 4–6
resources.title: Course Resources

modules.title: Briefs, strategy and the big idea
modules.banner: Use in this module: Ad Strategist skill · Workflow 01. Find them in Course Resources.
modules.description: A good AI ad starts with a good idea, not a good prompt.

doc.p:
Use
Ad Image Director (product shots) · Workflow 02, steps 1–3

Do this now
Make 4 packshots of your product from one phone photo.

items.desc: Packshots: a good reference photo is taken in daylight on a plain background with the label sharp. Attach the photo and use lighting words (softbox, rim light, gradient background).
items.title: Studio packshots from one photo

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Image Director (product shots) · Workflow 02, steps 1–3
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Image Director (product shots) · Workflow 02, step 5

Do this now
Make 4 lifestyle images that fit your brand.

items.desc: Lifestyle: put the product in scenes that fit the brand (vanity, Diwali, beach). Props tell the story.
items.title: Lifestyle scenes and backgrounds

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Image Director (product shots) · Workflow 02, step 5
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Image Director (accuracy check) · Workflow 02, step 4

Do this now
Check your best image with the accuracy check and fix anything wrong.

items.desc: Accuracy: zoom into the label every time. Fix it with one change per round in edit mode, regenerate, or paste the real label on in editing. Every image gets a verdict: SHIP, FIX or REGENERATE.
items.title: Keeping labels, logos and shape accurate

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Image Director (accuracy check) · Workflow 02, step 4
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Image Director (e-commerce set) · Workflow 02, step 5

Do this now
Make a 4-image e-commerce set: white background, infographic, scale shot, lifestyle.

items.desc: E-commerce set: white-background main image, infographic, scale shot, lifestyle shot.
items.title: E-commerce listing images

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Image Director (e-commerce set) · Workflow 02, step 5
resources.title: Course Resources

modules.title: AI product photography
modules.banner: Use in this module: Ad Image Director skill · Workflow 02. Find them in Course Resources.
modules.description: One phone photo can become a full studio shoot, as long as the label stays real.

doc.p:
Use
Ad Image Director (consistent model) · Workflow 02, step 6

Do this now
Make a character sheet for your brand model.

items.desc: Consistent model: make a character sheet (front, side, full body, expressions) and attach it every time.
items.title: Creating consistent AI models

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Image Director (consistent model) · Workflow 02, step 6
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Image Director (styling) · Workflow 02, step 6

Do this now
Style your model in 2 outfits with the garments' real colours.

items.desc: Styling: describe fabric, colour and fit exactly. Keep the garment's real colours.
items.title: Digital styling: fabric, colour and fit

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Image Director (styling) · Workflow 02, step 6
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Image Director (styling)

Do this now
Make one image with a correctly named outfit and a real setting from your market.

items.desc: Indian skin tones and outfits: don't let AI lighten skin. Name the real outfit (Banarasi saree, Chikankari kurta) and a real setting.
items.title: Indian skin tones, outfits and settings

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Image Director (styling)
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Image Director (sets & locations)

Do this now
Design one set and show it from 3 angles with the same light.

items.desc: Sets: mood board → one set → the same light in every shot.
items.title: Designing any set or location

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Image Director (sets & locations)
resources.title: Course Resources

modules.title: Models, styling and virtual sets
modules.banner: Use in this module: Ad Image Director skill · Workflow 02. Find them in Course Resources.
modules.description: Same face, same look, every shot. That's what makes it a brand.

doc.p:
Use
Ad Video Director (still → video) · Workflow 03, steps 1–4

Do this now
Turn your hero image into 3 clips with 3 different camera moves.

items.desc: Image to video: use your approved still as the start frame in Flow. Camera words: push-in, orbit, dolly, tilt. Make 2–3 takes and pick the best.
items.title: Image-to-video and camera moves

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Video Director (still → video) · Workflow 03, steps 1–4
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Video Director (multi-shot film) · Workflow 03, steps 1–4

Do this now
Make a 4-shot, 15s film from your storyboard.

items.desc: Multi-shot film: shot list → one keyframe per shot → one clip per shot. Keep the light, colour and wardrobe the same throughout.
items.title: Multi-shot stories that hold together

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Video Director (multi-shot film) · Workflow 03, steps 1–4
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Video Director (CGI & recipes)

Do this now
Make one CGI shot of your product.

items.desc: CGI without a 3D team: giant product in a city, splash explosions, impossible scale.
items.title: VFX and CGI shots without a 3D team

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Video Director (CGI & recipes)
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Video Director (CGI & recipes)

Do this now
Make one recipe clip for your category: food, fashion or tech.

items.desc: Recipes: food pour, fabric movement, tech reveal.
items.title: Food, fashion and tech video recipes

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Video Director (CGI & recipes)
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Video Director (voice, music & SFX) · Workflow 03, step 5

Do this now
Make a voiceover for your 15s script, in two languages if you can.

items.desc: Voiceover: write for the ear in short lines. In ElevenLabs, pick a voice and direct the pace and emotion. Hindi in Devanagari script is pronounced better.
items.title: Voiceovers and dubbing in Hindi and English

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Video Director (voice, music & SFX) · Workflow 03, step 5
resources.title: Course Resources

Use
Ad Video Director (voice, music & SFX) · Workflow 03, step 5

Do this now
Make a jingle and a 5-second sonic logo.

items.desc: Jingle: a Suno brief needs genre, tempo, mood and the brand name in the hook. Also make a 5-second sonic logo.
items.title: AI music and brand jingles

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Video Director (voice, music & SFX) · Workflow 03, step 5
resources.title: Course Resources

doc.p:
Use
Ad Video Director (voice, music & SFX)

Do this now
Make one short talking shot with clean lip-sync.

items.desc: Dialogue and lip-sync: use Flow's built-in audio for short lines, keep the lines short, and check the mouths.
items.title: Directing dialogue and lip-sync

resources.text: Skill and workflow for this lesson: Ad Video Director (voice, music & SFX)
resources.title: Course Resources

Use
Ad Video Director (voice, music & SFX) · Workflow 03, step 5

Do this now
Add sound effects to your 15s ad. Compare it silent and with full sound.

items.desc: Sound design: whoosh, pour, click, ASMR. Play the same ad silent, then with full sound.
items.title: Sound design that sells

Ad Video Director (AI UGC & ambassador) · Workflow 03, step 6

Create your AI creator: look, personality and voice.

items.desc: AI creator: handheld camera, a real room, natural light, imperfect speech. Use one consistent creator.

Finish your ambassador bible so the same person appears in every campaign.

items.desc: Brand face: an ambassador bible (look, personality, voice, wardrobe), so it's the same person every month.

Make one concept in 9:16, 4:5 and 1:1, with text inside the safe zones.

Set up your campaign in Ads Manager. Don't publish until you're ready to spend.

Paste your results (or the sample) into the Ad Strategist and plan round 2.

Use
Vibe Editor · Workflow 04, steps 1–3

Do this now
Vibe-edit your 15s or 30s ad with the Vibe Editor skill.

items.desc: The 5 steps are Dump → Vibe → Beat → Layer → Sound. A vibe prompt has 5 parts: platform + length + energy + look + goal.
items.title: Editing ads that hold attention

Vibe Editor (end cards) · Workflow 04, steps 4–5

Add a 3-second end card with your logo, CTA and offer, then export 3 ratios.

items.desc: End card: logo + one CTA + the offer, for 2–3 seconds.
items.title: Logo, text and CTA end cards

description: Learn to make product shoots, model shoots, video ads, UGC and Meta ads with AI, from the first brief to a launched campaign. 11 modules and 41 lessons, 4 skills you attach to Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini that write your prompts for you, and 4 step-by-step workflows. You finish with a full campaign for your portfolio, and you learn how to price and pitch AI ad services.
